findings.description: The security group allows inbound TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH on a publicly-addressed instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or exploitation attempts against the management port.

findings.issue_category: hard-coded cloud credentials in user data
findings.description: The user_data script exports a static AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY. EC2 user data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by any local process or via SSRF against the public web server, leaking long-lived AWS credentials.

No metadata_options block is set, so IMDSv1 (token-optional) remains enabled on an internet-facing Apache host, making retrieval of user data and any role credentials via SSRF against 169.254.169.254 trivial.
The instance defines no root_block_device with encrypted = true, so unless the AMI or account default enforces it the root volume is stored unencrypted at rest.
The EBS volume attached to the web server does not set encrypted = true or a KMS key, so its data is stored unencrypted.

The VPC flow log bucket declares no server-side encryption configuration (no aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration resource), so sensitive network telemetry is stored without an explicit encryption control or customer-managed key.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for the flow-log bucket, so it relies solely on account-level defaults to prevent a future ACL or policy from exposing network traffic records publicly.
The bucket has no policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, permitting cleartext HTTP access to stored flow log data.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true combined with the 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway means every instance launched here, including portal_server, is directly internet-reachable with no bastion, NAT, or load balancer boundary.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true and association with the internet-gateway route table mean all instances in this subnet are automatically assigned public IPs; there is no private subnet tier for backend workloads.
The egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing a compromised host to exfiltrate data or reach command-and-control infrastructure without restriction.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and the user_data installs plain Apache with no TLS listener or terminating load balancer, so all portal traffic is transmitted in cleartext.
